rows.issue: No measured core at or below 10 kg/m3 meets the wrinkling need with 6061 faces on the P2 float ceiling.
rows.numbers: Best measured: meza2014-hollow-alumina-octet-lightest-E at 5.5 kg/m3, Ec*Gc margin 0.000171 on the least-factor split (gap 5.84e+03, 18 on stress; 1.66e+03 at the classical 0.76), gap 1.7e+04 on the buckling split. Band 1-4 kg/m3: kashani2019-npg-3-tension, gap 7.57e+04 (2.16e+04 classical).
rows.closes_when: a measured core's Ec*Gc at its own density meets the need on its row; or a face change lowers the need, which scales as sigma_face^3/E_face (008b's face table); or a wrinkling test on a representative sandwich replaces the CR-1457 design coefficient.

rows.issue: No source measured a transverse shear modulus for any core at or below 10 kg/m3.
rows.numbers: Gc is DERIVED as Ec/2 (isotropic, nu = 0, the optimistic bound) for every non-honeycomb core; at nu = 1/3 every product falls by 0.75 and every crimp margin by 0.75. Si et al. 2014 measured shear stress at 9.6 kg/m3 but printed no modulus.
rows.closes_when: a plate-shear or sandwich-beam shear modulus is measured on a candidate core.

rows.issue: On the least-factor split no measured core at or below 10 kg/m3 reaches the crimp shear modulus.
rows.numbers: Need 2.52e+06 Pa at 1 to 9.6 kg/m3; best meza2014-hollow-alumina-octet-lightest-E margin 0.735 (gap 1.36) on the derived Gc. On the buckling split three alumina lattice points pass (0.3, 5.3, 5.5 kg/m3), the 0.3 point on a 6 m core.
rows.closes_when: a measured Gc above the need on the row the design uses.

rows.issue: Most ultralight strengths are not crush strengths: stress at 80 percent strain (Qiu 2012), undefined 'max stress' (Si 2014), ultimate stress of undefined strain (Xu 2019), 40 percent compression (Basotect), indentation or tension (Kashani 2019). These can fail the crush check but never pass it.
rows.numbers: The only structural pass at or below 10 kg/m3 is meza2015-hier-hollow-alumina-heaviest-halfcell at 5.3 kg/m3, margin 1.34, read by eye from a plot (about 25 percent) with its density inferred from relative density times 2900 kg/m3.
rows.closes_when: a small-strain collapse or yield strength is measured at the candidate density.

rows.issue: This card sourced no core between 53 and 190 kg/m3, so the lightest core passing all three is bounded, not found.
rows.numbers: The only pass is jacobsen2011-vitreous-carbon-octet-0p19 at 190 kg/m3 (secondary source); at that density the float-ceiling core is 9.2 mm thick and the shell's buckling SF is 0.0204 at kd 0.2.
rows.closes_when: mid-density cores are sourced (for example high-density PMI foams, end-grain balsa, carbon micro-lattices from 50 to 190 kg/m3) and run through compute.py.

rows.issue: Two values arrive second-hand: the vitreous carbon octet micro-lattice (Jacobsen 2011, via Zhang 2019) and the glassy carbon exponents (Bauer 2016, via Zhang 2019); Schaedler 2011's 10 kg/m3 nickel point also via Zhang 2019.
rows.numbers: The 190 kg/m3 all-three pass rests on the secondary Jacobsen numbers (1.1 GPa, 10.2 MPa).
rows.closes_when: the primary papers are opened and the values matched.

rows.issue: Maloney 2013, Zheng 2016, Meza 2014, Meza 2015 and Zhu 2015 values are read by eye from log plots (about 25 to 50 percent); the Meza densities are inferred from relative density.
rows.numbers: None of these readings sits near a margin of 1 except the Meza 2015 crush point (1.34).
rows.closes_when: tabulated values (journal SI or theses) replace the readings.

rows.issue: The continuum wrinkling form assumes a core finer than the wrinkle wavelength; lattice cell sizes were not sourced. Intracell dimpling, a fourth local mode outside the card's three, is reported beside them.
rows.numbers: CR-1457 eq 2.1-4 with the straight-line biaxial rule allows cells up to 3.52 mm above 9.6 kg/m3 and up to 9.84 mm on the least-factor split at 0.1 kg/m3; every honeycomb cell in the table fails it except the 1/8-inch (1.11).
rows.closes_when: cell sizes are sourced and a wrinkling model valid at that cell scale is applied.

rows.issue: CR-1457 eq 2.2-14 at these core-to-face ratios (tc/tf about 220 to 560) is far outside its test data; it makes the honeycomb need an Ec no honeycomb has.
rows.numbers: Ec needed 1.03e+10 to 7.74e+10 Pa; best honeycomb margin 0.00462 (gap 216).
rows.closes_when: a symmetric-wrinkling model or test for very thick honeycomb cores, or a honeycomb with a stabilising foam fill.

rows.issue: The 6061 face is past its QUESTIONABLE 276 MPa on every row, so the elastic wrinkling forms (eta 1) flatter it.
rows.numbers: Face stress 3.57e+08 Pa (Q, 0.1 kg/m3) to 7.09e+08 Pa.
rows.closes_when: the face material changes (008b) or CR-1457 section 9 plasticity factors are applied.

rows.issue: On the buckling split the core exceeds a tenth of the radius below about 1.8 kg/m3 and the radius itself below about 0.18 kg/m3, so B-split margins there are not physical (external-area and thin-shell rules).
rows.numbers: B core 1.81 m at 1 kg/m3, 18.1 m at 0.1 kg/m3; the Q split holds h = 0.18907 m and is valid at every density.
rows.closes_when: a thick-shell sandwich model with the inner surface area replaces the external-area rule.

rows.issue: The ideal stretch-dominated lattice (Ashby 2006 eq 5.1, Gc = Ec/2) is a bound, not a material; strength is not projected because no strut-buckling constant was sourced.
rows.numbers: Passes wrinkling and crimp on the least-factor split from 1.34 (K13D2U-grade), 2.46 (CNT yarn), 4.82 (beryllium), 25.3 (alumina), 55.9 kg/m3 (6061). At 5 kg/m3 a lattice needs 0.378, 0.628 and 0.982 of ideal; measured alumina lattices reach 0.0279 to 0.0422.
rows.closes_when: a lattice of a fibre-grade strut material is built and measured at 1 to 8 kg/m3.

rows.issue: The wrinkling-precision gap, carried as 009 and 014 carry it: design coefficients (continuum 0.50, CR-1457 eq 2.2-5; honeycomb 0.33, eq 2.2-14) against classical ones (0.76, NASA/CR-1999-208994 Table 3; 0.82, eq 2.2-12).
rows.numbers: The product need falls to 0.285 at 0.76 (a factor 3.51); the honeycomb Ec need falls to 0.162 at 0.82 (6.17). No verdict in this card moves.
rows.closes_when: a representative wrinkling test fixes the coefficient for the chosen face and core.

rows.issue: The p/2 core-stress model is the brief's own example, QUESTIONABLE; local face bending is ignored.
rows.closes_when: a sandwich-sphere through-thickness solution replaces it.

rows.issue: EPS strengths are specification minima at 1, 5 or 10 percent strain, and the sheets disagree.
rows.numbers: EPS12 (11.2 kg/m3): 15 kPa at 1 percent and 40 kPa at 10 percent (ASTM D6817 minima, margins 0.314 and 0.838); 34 kPa at 10 percent (older C578 minimum, 0.712); 005b's National Polystyrene 50 kPa at 11 kg/m3 gave 1.05.
rows.closes_when: the design adopts one strain definition and a measured (not minimum) value.

rows.issue: Every lattice and aerogel in this table was tested as a laboratory specimen (micrometres to centimetres); the float-ceiling core is about 1257 m2 by 0.19 m. The commercial foams (EPS, melamine, polyimide) are made at larger scale but fail the checks by orders of magnitude. Vacuum outgassing, creep under a sustained p/2 (polymer foams), and temperature were not assessed.
rows.numbers: No lattice or aerogel source here reports a manufacturing route at metre scale.
rows.closes_when: a manufacturing route at metre scale is sourced for a candidate core.

rows.issue: Sources that were paywalled or blocked, so none of their values is used: Schaedler 2011 full text and SI, Torrents 2012, Valdevit 2013, Salari-Sharif 2014, Zheng 2014 (Science 344, 1373), Jang 2013, Deshpande-Ashby-Fleck 2001, Gross and Fricke 1995, Woignier 1989 full text, Ma 2000 full text, Sun 2013, Hu 2013, Zou 2010, Gui 2010, Worsley 2009 and 2012, Mecklenburg 2012, Eckel 2016, Bauer 2016, Jacobsen 2011.
rows.numbers: Zheng 2014 (MIT DSpace HTTP 429, Science 403) is the likeliest source of a stiffer ultralight ceramic octet point.
rows.closes_when: those texts are obtained and their values added through build_cores.py.
